articles.title: The Life of a Butterfly
articles.content: A butterfly starts as a tiny egg. The egg hatches into a caterpillar. The caterpillar eats leaves and grows. Then it makes a chrysalis. Inside, it changes into a butterfly. This change is called metamorphosis.

questions.question: What does a butterfly start as?

articles.audio_narration_script: A butterfly begins as a tiny egg. It hatches into a caterpillar that eats leaves. Then it forms a chrysalis and changes into a butterfly. This amazing change is called metamorphosis.

articles.title: Why We Need Water
articles.content: Water is important for all living things. People drink water to stay healthy. Plants need water to grow. Animals drink water too. We use water to cook and clean.

questions.question: What is one way we use water?

articles.audio_narration_script: Water helps people, plants, and animals. We drink it to stay healthy. Plants use it to grow. We also use water for cooking and cleaning.

articles.title: All About the Sun
articles.content: The Sun is a big star. It gives us light and heat. Plants use sunlight to grow. The Earth moves around the Sun.

questions.question: What does the Sun give us?

articles.audio_narration_script: The Sun is a bright star. It gives us light and keeps us warm. The Earth travels around the Sun every year.

articles.title: The Five Senses
articles.content: We have five senses. We see with our eyes. We hear with our ears. We smell with our nose. We taste with our tongue. We touch with our skin.

questions.question: How many senses do we have?
What do we use to hear?
What do we use to taste?

articles.audio_narration_script: Our five senses help us learn about the world. We see, hear, smell, taste, and touch every day.

articles.title: Rain and the Water Cycle
articles.content: The Sun heats water in lakes and oceans. The water turns into vapor and goes into the sky. It forms clouds. When clouds get heavy, rain falls. This is called the water cycle.
articles.audio_narration_script: The Sun warms water and turns it into vapor. It forms clouds in the sky. When clouds are heavy, rain falls. This is the water cycle.

articles.title: Mammals
articles.content: Mammals are animals that have hair or fur. They drink milk from their mothers when they are babies. Most mammals give birth to live babies. Dogs, cats, and whales are mammals.
articles.audio_narration_script: Mammals are animals with hair or fur. Baby mammals drink milk from their mothers. Dogs, cats, and even whales are mammals.

articles.title: Birds
articles.content: Birds have feathers and wings. Most birds can fly. They lay eggs. Birds use their beaks to eat food.

questions.question: What do birds use to eat?

articles.audio_narration_script: Birds have feathers and wings. Many birds can fly. They lay eggs and use their beaks to eat.

articles.title: Reptiles
articles.content: Reptiles are cold-blooded animals. They have dry, scaly skin. Snakes, lizards, and turtles are reptiles. Most reptiles lay eggs.

questions.question: What kind of skin do reptiles have?

articles.audio_narration_script: Reptiles have dry, scaly skin. Snakes and turtles are reptiles. They are cold-blooded animals.

articles.title: Fish
articles.content: Fish live in water. They breathe through gills. Fish have fins to swim. Most fish lay eggs.
articles.audio_narration_script: Fish live in water. They breathe with gills and swim using fins.

articles.title: Plants Need Sunlight
articles.content: Plants need sunlight to make food. They also need water and air. Leaves help plants take in sunlight. Roots hold plants in the ground.

questions.question: What do plants need to make food?
What holds a plant in the ground?

articles.audio_narration_script: Plants need sunlight, water, and air. Leaves catch sunlight. Roots keep the plant in the ground.

articles.title: The Moon
articles.content: The Moon moves around the Earth. It shines at night because it reflects sunlight. The Moon changes shape in the sky. These changes are called phases.

questions.question: What does the Moon move around?
What are the Moon’s shape changes called?

articles.audio_narration_script: The Moon travels around Earth. It shines because it reflects sunlight. The Moon has different phases.

articles.title: The Four Seasons
articles.content: There are four seasons: spring, summer, autumn, and winter. In spring, flowers grow. Summer is warm. In autumn, leaves fall. Winter is cold.

questions.question: In which season do leaves fall?

articles.audio_narration_script: We have four seasons. Spring has flowers. Summer is warm. Autumn has falling leaves. Winter is cold.

articles.title: Healthy Food
articles.content: Healthy food helps our bodies grow strong. Fruits and vegetables are healthy. Drinking water is important. Eating too much sugar is not healthy.

questions.question: What helps our bodies grow strong?
What should we not eat too much of?

articles.audio_narration_script: Healthy foods like fruits and vegetables help us grow strong. Too much sugar is not good for our bodies.

articles.title: Teeth Care
articles.content: We use our teeth to chew food. We should brush our teeth twice a day. Brushing keeps teeth clean and strong. Visiting the dentist helps keep teeth healthy.

questions.question: What do we use teeth for?
How many times should we brush daily?

articles.audio_narration_script: Teeth help us chew food. We should brush twice a day and visit the dentist to keep them healthy.

articles.title: Community Helpers
articles.content: Community helpers are people who help us every day. Teachers help us learn. Doctors help us stay healthy. Firefighters keep us safe.

questions.question: Who keeps us safe from fires?

articles.audio_narration_script: Community helpers make our lives better. Teachers teach us. Doctors care for us. Firefighters protect us.

articles.title: The Solar System
articles.content: The Solar System is made up of the Sun and eight planets. The planets move around the Sun. Earth is one of these planets. Each planet is different.

questions.question: How many planets are in the Solar System?

articles.audio_narration_script: The Solar System has the Sun and eight planets. The planets travel around the Sun. Earth is one of these planets.

articles.title: Dinosaurs
articles.content: Dinosaurs lived on Earth millions of years ago. Some were big and some were small. Some ate plants and others ate meat. Dinosaurs are now extinct.
articles.audio_narration_script: Dinosaurs lived millions of years ago. Some ate plants and some ate meat. Today, dinosaurs are extinct.

articles.title: Insects
articles.content: Insects are small animals with six legs. Most insects have wings. Ants, bees, and butterflies are insects. Insects have three body parts.

questions.question: How many legs do insects have?
How many body parts do insects have?

articles.audio_narration_script: Insects are small animals with six legs. Ants and bees are insects. They have three body parts.

articles.title: Magnets
articles.content: Magnets can pull some metal objects. This pull is called magnetism. Magnets can push or pull other magnets. Not all metals stick to magnets.

questions.question: Do all metals stick to magnets?

articles.audio_narration_script: Magnets can pull some metal objects. This pull is called magnetism. Not all metals stick to magnets.

articles.title: Habitats
articles.content: A habitat is a place where an animal lives. Forests, oceans, and deserts are habitats. Animals live in habitats that meet their needs.

questions.question: What is a habitat?
options: A place where an animal lives

questions.question: Why do animals live in habitats?

articles.audio_narration_script: A habitat is a place where animals live. Forests and oceans are habitats. Animals choose habitats that help them survive.

articles.title: Air
articles.content: Air is all around us. We cannot see it, but we can feel it. We need air to breathe. Wind is moving air.
articles.audio_narration_script: Air is everywhere. We need it to breathe. When air moves, we call it wind.

articles.title: Rocks
articles.content: Rocks are natural materials found on Earth. Some rocks are hard and some are soft. Rocks can be different colors and sizes.
articles.audio_narration_script: Rocks are found all over Earth. They can be big or small, hard or soft, and many different colors.

articles.title: Transportation
articles.content: Transportation helps people move from place to place. Cars, buses, trains, and airplanes are types of transportation.

questions.question: What does transportation help us do?

articles.audio_narration_script: Transportation helps us travel. Cars, buses, trains, and airplanes take us from place to place.

articles.title: The Human Heart
articles.content: The heart is a muscle inside your body. It pumps blood. Blood carries oxygen and nutrients to all parts of the body.
articles.audio_narration_script: Your heart is a strong muscle. It pumps blood through your body. Blood carries oxygen and nutrients.

articles.title: Shadows
articles.content: A shadow forms when light is blocked. The Sun can make shadows. Shadows change size during the day.

questions.question: Do shadows stay the same size?

articles.audio_narration_script: Shadows form when light is blocked. The Sun makes shadows. Shadows can change size during the day.

articles.title: Frogs
articles.content: Frogs are amphibians. They can live on land and in water. Frogs start life as tadpoles. They change as they grow.

questions.question: What kind of animal is a frog?
What do baby frogs start as?

articles.audio_narration_script: Frogs are amphibians. They live on land and in water. Baby frogs are called tadpoles.

articles.title: Volcanoes
articles.content: A volcano is an opening in the Earth. It can erupt with lava. Lava is hot melted rock.

questions.question: What comes out of a volcano?

articles.audio_narration_script: A volcano can erupt with hot lava. Lava is melted rock from inside the Earth.

articles.title: Bees
articles.content: Bees are insects. They collect nectar from flowers. Bees make honey. They help plants grow by pollination.
articles.audio_narration_script: Bees collect nectar from flowers. They make honey and help plants grow by pollination.

articles.title: The Skeleton
articles.content: The skeleton is made of bones. It helps our body stand up. Bones protect important organs like the brain and heart.

questions.question: What is the skeleton made of?
What does the skeleton help us do?

articles.audio_narration_script: Your skeleton is made of bones. It helps you stand up and protects important organs.

articles.title: The Ocean
articles.content: The ocean is a large body of salt water. Many animals live in the ocean. The ocean covers most of Earth’s surface.

questions.question: What kind of water is in the ocean?
Do animals live in the ocean?
Does the ocean cover much of Earth?

articles.audio_narration_script: The ocean is full of salt water. Many animals live there. The ocean covers most of our planet.
